title: Oracle
explorerSubtitle: Run procedures, functions, packages, and queries generated by Generate Service.
personasSubtitle: CRUD built on gsSpGetPersonas, gsSpInsertPersona, gsSpUpdatePersona, and gsSpDeletePersona.
emptyRequest: This endpoint does not require a request body.
executeToSeeResponse: Run the endpoint to see the response.

operationDescriptions.default: This case demonstrates how Generate Service publishes an Oracle operation as a REST endpoint while respecting the PL/SQL signature or defined query.
operationDescriptions.gsSpGetTwoCursors: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can expose an Oracle procedure with multiple SYS_REFCURSOR outputs and return personas and children as separate REST results.
operationDescriptions.gsSpGetPersonasCursor: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can publish an output SYS_REFCURSOR as a REST list of Oracle records.
operationDescriptions.gsSpArraysPrimitivosInout: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can handle Oracle primitive collections with IN, IN OUT, and OUT parameters inside one REST contract.
operationDescriptions.gsSpTypeParams: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can interpret %TYPE parameters and publish scalar outputs aligned with Oracle table columns.
operationDescriptions.gsSpCountPersonasCursor: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can receive a cursor as input, process it in PL/SQL, and return a calculated result.
operationDescriptions.gsSpInsertPersona: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can receive an Oracle object type from REST, run an insert, and return the generated id.
operationDescriptions.gsSpUpdatePersona: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can use a full object type to update Oracle data and return a result confirmation.
operationDescriptions.gsSpDeletePersona: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can publish a PL/SQL delete by id and return the result to the REST consumer.
operationDescriptions.gsSpGetPersona: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can retrieve an entity by id and return it as an Oracle object type transformed into a REST object.
operationDescriptions.gsSpLobValues: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can receive and return CLOB/BLOB values, allowing Oracle to process text and binary content within the REST flow.
operationDescriptions.gsSpGetThreeCursors: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can expose procedures with three independent cursors and organize each result set in the REST response.
operationDescriptions.gsSpGetPersonasDetalle: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can publish Oracle collections with nested objects, returning personas with related address and children.
operationDescriptions.gsSpCursorInWithOutputs: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can combine an input cursor with additional outputs, returning counts and a new cursor in one call.
operationDescriptions.gsSpLobCursor: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can return CLOB/BLOB values inside an Oracle cursor and present them as data consumable from REST.
operationDescriptions.gsSpArraysPrimitivosOut: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can map multiple OUT collections of Oracle primitive types into a structured REST response.
operationDescriptions.gsSpCursorOutNoMetadata: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can handle cursors whose structure is known when the operation runs and still deliver the result to the client.
operationDescriptions.gsSpLobInout: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can handle CLOB/BLOB values as IN OUT parameters, receiving content and returning the version transformed by Oracle.
operationDescriptions.gsSpGetPersonas: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can publish the Oracle GS_PERSONA_TAB collection as a REST list of objects.
operationDescriptions.gsSpGetPersonaDetalle: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can retrieve a specific entity with nested data and deliver it as a composite REST object.
operationDescriptions.gsSpCursorInoutPersonas: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can consume an IN OUT cursor, process its rows, and replace it with a new output cursor.
operationDescriptions.gsFnCountPersonas: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can expose a no-input Oracle function and return its scalar value as a simple REST response.
operationDescriptions.gsFnTypeNombre: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can publish a function with a %TYPE parameter and return a scalar value aligned with the Oracle table.
operationDescriptions.gsFnPipePersonas: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can expose a pipelined function and convert its emitted rows into a REST collection.
operationDescriptions.gsFnGetPersonasTab: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can publish a function returning a typed Oracle collection and deliver it as a REST list.
operationDescriptions.gsFnCursorInoutPersonas: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can combine an IN OUT cursor with a scalar return value inside an Oracle function exposed by REST.
operationDescriptions.gsFnCursorReturnWithOut: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can expose a function that returns a cursor and also provides OUT parameters in the same REST response.
operationDescriptions.gsFnGetPersonasCursor: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can publish an Oracle function returning SYS_REFCURSOR and convert it into a REST list.
operationDescriptions.gsFnCursorInCount: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can receive a cursor in an Oracle function and return a scalar calculation based on its rows.
operationDescriptions.gsFnGetPersonaObj: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can expose a function returning an Oracle object type as a REST object.
operationDescriptions.fnCountPersonas: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can publish functions inside Oracle packages while keeping the same REST consumption model as standalone functions.
operationDescriptions.pipePersonas: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can expose pipelined functions from Oracle packages and return collections filtered by state.
operationDescriptions.getPersonasCursor: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can publish package procedures returning cursors as REST lists.
operationDescriptions.getPersona: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can consume package procedures returning object types and deliver them as REST objects.
operationDescriptions.fnGetPersonasCursor: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can expose package functions returning Oracle cursors as REST collections.
operationDescriptions.arraysPrimitivosInout: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can handle primitive IN OUT collections from an Oracle package with the same generated REST contract.
operationDescriptions.cursorInWithOutputs: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can expose package procedures that combine an input cursor, an output cursor, and calculated values.
operationDescriptions.gsQUpdatePersonass: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can turn a parameterized UPDATE query into a REST write endpoint over Oracle.
operationDescriptions.gsQPersonasTotalHijosWith: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can publish analytical queries with WITH, JOIN, and aggregations as REST responses.
operationDescriptions.gsQDeletePersona: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can expose a parameterized DELETE query and return an execution confirmation.
operationDescriptions.gsQPersonasActivasWith: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can publish Oracle queries with WITH to filter data and return it as a REST collection.
operationDescriptions.gsQPersonasByCityJoinss: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can expose JOIN queries to relate personas and addresses through a business filter.
operationDescriptions.gsQInsertPersonaSelect: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can publish an INSERT SELECT that creates new records from existing data.
operationDescriptions.gsQPersonaByNombre: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can expose parameterized name-search queries as REST endpoints.
operationDescriptions.gsQPersonaById: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can publish a parameterized query to retrieve an Oracle entity by id.
operationDescriptions.gsQInsertPersona: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can turn a parameterized INSERT query into a REST creation endpoint.

support.title: Oracle Support
support.subtitle: General guide to what Generate Service can expose from Oracle and how it transforms PL/SQL, queries, and Oracle types into Java and REST.
support.capabilitiesSubtitle: Oracle can publish procedures, functions, packages, queries, cursors, object types, table types, LOBs, and pipelined functions as generated REST endpoints.
support.typeMappingTitle: Oracle types supported by Generate Service
support.typeMappingSubtitle: This table crosses the official Oracle 11g R2 types used by the project environment with the Generate Service type rule. Oracle types not shown here are outside this scope until they have an explicit mapping.
support.numberPrecisionSubtitle: Generate Service classifies NUMBER by precision and scale, then uses that classification to produce the Java counterpart in the contract.
support.typeMappingNote: Oracle 11g R2 does not have a SQL JSON or BOOLEAN type. In this documentation, boolean comes from NUMBER(1,0) classified by Generate Service; official types such as NCHAR, NVARCHAR2, NCLOB, BINARY_FLOAT, BINARY_DOUBLE, INTERVAL, ROWID, UROWID, BFILE, XMLType, and LONG RAW are not documented as supported because they do not explicitly cross with the current rule.
support.primitiveNote: By default Generate Service generates contracts with the direct Java equivalent, such as boolean, int, long, float, double, or BigDecimal according to the Oracle type or NUMBER precision and scale. That contract can be adjusted to wrappers such as Integer, Boolean, Long, Float, or Double when the case requires it.
support.listWrapperNote: Single-attribute lists use object types because Java does not support List<int> or List<boolean>. In those cases Generate Service produces List<Integer>, List<Boolean>, List<Double>, List<String>, and similar shapes.
support.modelingSubtitle: OBJECT represents an Oracle TYPE AS OBJECT and is modeled as a structured DTO. TABLE represents a TYPE AS TABLE OF and is modeled as an ArrayList or List of the corresponding type.
support.rulesSubtitle: These rules apply to the generated microservice and keep the customer-facing contract stable.

procedures.title: Procedures
procedures.description: Supports procedures with IN, OUT, and IN OUT parameters, including scalars, object types, collections, LOBs, and SYS_REFCURSOR.

functions.title: Functions
functions.description: Supports functions with scalar, OBJECT, TABLE, and SYS_REFCURSOR returns, plus OUT parameters when the engine allows them.

packages.title: Packages
packages.description: Can expose procedures and functions declared inside Oracle packages while preserving the technical package/member name.

queries.title: Queries
queries.description: Supports parameterized SELECT and DML queries such as INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE, including JOIN, WITH, and aggregates.

pipelined.title: Pipelined functions
pipelined.description: Can expose pipelined functions that return TABLE types as REST array responses.

cursors.title: SYS_REFCURSOR
cursors.description: Supports OUT, IN, and IN OUT cursors for transporting tabular results between Oracle and the REST endpoint.

objectTypes.title: Object types
objectTypes.description: An Oracle TYPE AS OBJECT represents a data structure and becomes a Java DTO exposed as a JSON object.

tableTypes.title: Table types
tableTypes.description: A TYPE AS TABLE OF represents an Oracle collection and becomes an ArrayList or List of the matching DTO or simple type.

lobs.title: CLOB and BLOB
lobs.description: Supports CLOB as text and BLOB/RAW as binary content serialized for REST transport.

objectToDto.title: OBJECT to DTO
objectToDto.description: Each object type attribute becomes a field in the generated DTO.

tableToArray.title: TABLE OF OBJECT to ArrayList
tableToArray.description: An Oracle collection of objects is exposed as a JSON array of DTOs.

simpleTableToList.title: TABLE OF simple type to List<T>
simpleTableToList.description: Collections of simple values use Java wrappers so they can be represented as lists.

rules.snakeCase: In Oracle, snake_case is recommended for parameters, variables, and PL/SQL names.
rules.camelCase: Generate Service transforms Oracle names to camelCase for Java and REST contracts.
rules.endpointNames: PL/SQL names become generated method names and REST endpoint names.
rules.envOverride: The per-engine base URL is configured from .env with API_ENDPOINT_ORACLE; when it is not set, the UI falls back to http://localhost:8083. Backend REST endpoint paths can also be changed with environment variables.
rules.jsonProperty: Variable names exposed in JSON can be adjusted with the Jackson @JsonProperty annotation.

rules.repositoryIntegrity: After the microservice is generated, Generate Service validates the integrity of generated repositories.
rules.licenseValidation: The generated API includes local integrity and license validations through a secure token issued by Generate Service. These validations run inside the generated API itself and do not require calls to external licensing services.
rules.signedMetadata: Do not modify @Callable, @SpParameter, types, inputs, outputs, PL/SQL names, or signed queries.
rules.regenerateOnSourceChange: If the data source, procedure, function, package, query, parameters, or types change, the microservice must be regenerated.
rules.oneEndpointPerSource: Each PL/SQL unit or query the customer wants to consume should be generated as its own stable API source.

rules.controllers: Controllers can add validation, input adaptation, or response enrichment.
rules.services: Services can add business logic before or after invoking the generated source.
rules.businessLogic: Responses can be recalculated, composed, or transformed without changing signed metadata.
rules.sourceLock: The generated data source is protected: repositories, signatures, parameters, and query/PLSQL definitions are not manually changed.
